title: Adopter prioritization — Lighthouse rubric for SDK language/auth/stream ergonomics
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a lightweight, reproducible intake and prioritization rubric ('Lighthouse') for SDK and client-library requests coming from enterprise customers and platform adopters. Focus areas: language support gaps, authentication patterns (OAuth2 / SAML / token rotation / per-request KMS signatures), and streaming ergonomics (resumability, partial-response semantics, backpressure).

Context:
We are seeing repeated enterprise asks and partner onboarding friction tied to 3 recurring dimensions: 1) missing language bindings in critical JVM/.NET ecosystems, 2) unclear token rotation and role-based auth patterns for long-lived streams, and 3) streaming ergonomics that break when customers require resumability or server-initiated events over WebSocket/gRPC. PMs, Solutions, and SEs have been triaging ad-hoc. We need a reproducible decision process to: a) prioritize which language bindings to build/maintain, b) define minimal auth contracts/examples to satisfy enterprise SSO/KMS needs, and c) size streaming work by ergonomics risk.

Scope in this ticket:
- Define scoring rubric and thresholds for "Lighthouse" prioritization.
- Validate rubric against a prioritized list of 12 recent customer asks (sample included below).
- Produce a short PRD with recommended top-3 engineering scopes (e.g., Python+Node streaming ergonomics, Java SDK auth-shim, .NET minimal binding).
- Identify instrumentation signals for intake (MAU, number of concurrent streams, revenue, regulated industry).

Out-of-scope:
- Implementation work (actual SDK code) — tracked in ENG sub-issues.

Sample intake (12 asks):
[1] Large fintech: Java SDK + SAML SSO + token rotation for long-running market feed (50 concurrent streams).
[2] Healthtech customer: Python SDK + HIPAA audit logs + KMS envelope encryption for client secrets.
[3] ML platform team: Rust binding for on-prem Redwood Private (air-gapped).
[4] Enterprise search vendor: Node streaming errors semantics + reconnect/resume behavior.
[5] Internal solutions team: .NET binding for Windows-first customers.
[6] Marketplace partner: JS/Browser examples for ephemeral keys and token refresh.
[7] E-commerce: SDK telemetry hooks for per-request cost attribution.
[8] Regulated services: SAML/OAuth hybrid for delegated admin model.
[9] Gaming startup: low-latency streaming over UDP/QUIC prototypes.
[10] Research lab: Go SDK for embeddings and batch pipelines.
[11] Telecom: server-initiated events over streaming RPCs + backpressure.
[12] Large retail: nodejs streaming + resumability + automatic chunk-ack semantics.

Rubric (Lighthouse scoring):
- Demand (0-5): measured by number of customers/orgs requesting + MAU signal.
- Revenue/Strategic (0-5): contract value or partner signal (strategic partnership).
- Regulatory/Compliance risk (0-5): HIPAA/PCI/FINRA etc.
- Engineering lift (0-5, inverted): lower score if high lift — we favor small-ship wins.
- Security complexity (0-5): SSO/KMS needs that require deep infra changes (higher = more complex).
- Streaming risk multiplier (x1 or x1.5): if request includes resumability/partial semantics/backpressure, multiply final score by 1.5.

Scoring example (Large fintech Java SAML request):
- Demand 4, Revenue 5, Reg/Compliance 4, Eng lift 2, Security 4 => base = 19, streaming multiplier 1 => final 19.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
1) Lighthouse rubric documented and stored in Confluence (link below).
2) All 12 sample asks scored and ranked with rationales.
3) Top-3 recommended initiatives with estimated NRE (engineering points) and proposed release target.
4) Onboarding checklist for incoming requests (data points to capture: concurrent streams, expected session TTL, auth type, MAU, customer tier, compliance requirements).
5) Stakeholder sign-off from Solutions (Marco Alvarez), Security (Samir Patel), and Design (Anya Kuznetsova).

Decisions made so far:
- We will prioritize small-surface, high-signal wins (Python streaming ergonomics + Node resumability examples) before larger platform SDKs.
- For enterprise auth, we'll standardize on two deliverables: 1) an "auth-shim" pattern (thin adapter + example) for SAML/OAuth flows and token rotation; 2) an audit-log template customers can drop into their existing SIEM.
- Streaming: adopt a canonical resume token pattern (server issues opaque resume token per stream checkpoint) and include a minimal ack/seq number envelope in SDK transports.

Next steps (owner tags):
- Jordan Lee (PM) to finalize rubric and publish Confluence draft by 2026-03-15.
- Jordan + ENG leads to map top-3 to ENG-IDs and create rough point estimates by 2026-03-19.
- Solutions (Marco) to surface top-5 customers for early beta and coordinate NDA/PS engagement.
- Security (Samir) to review the auth-shim checklist and call out required infra changes (KMS integration, per-request signing) — due 2026-03-22.
- Design (Anya) to produce a single-page SDK ergonomics guideline for streaming (wireframes + API surface) by 2026-03-26.
